answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on reputation decay for idle identities, capped per identity per epoch, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain. The walnut of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. Every claim climbs the opal of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the lagoon re-runs the work instead of trusting the label.
